steps: Identify the 3D shape and pick the correct formula (cones, spheres and pyramids are on the formula sheet).
Substitute carefully: radius not diameter, perpendicular height not slant.
Give units: cm³ for volume, cm² for surface area.
Composite solids: split into basic shapes, then add or subtract.
method_card.title: Volume & Surface Area
method_card.content:
Prism: V = area of cross-section × length. Cuboid: V = \(lwh\), SA = \(2(lw+lh+wh)\). Cylinder: V = \(\pi r^2 h\), SA = \(2\pi r^2+2\pi rh\).

Cone: V = \(\frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h\). Sphere: V = \(\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3\), SA = \(4\pi r^2\). Pyramid: V = \(\frac{1}{3}\times\) base area \(\times h\).
method_card.example:
Volume of a cylinder: radius 4 cm, height 10 cm.

\(V = \pi(4)^2(10) = 160\pi \approx 502.7\) cm³.

steps: Composite solid: split into basic shapes, find each part, then add (joined) or subtract (a piece removed).
Keep each part in multiples of π until the final line, then round once.
Rearrange: to find a length from a given volume or area, substitute and solve, cancelling π where you can.
gold.title: Gold: composite solids and rearranging formulae

example.question: A hemisphere has radius 3 cm. Find the volume to 1 d.p.

steps: Cuboid: volume = length × width × height. Cube: volume = side³.
Prism: volume = cross-section area × length. Cylinder: volume = π r² h.
Surface area: add every face. A cuboid is 2(lw + lh + wh); a cube is 6 × side².
bronze.title: Bronze: volume and surface area of basic solids

example.question: Find the volume of a cuboid 4 cm × 3 cm × 5 cm.

steps: Cone: V = ⅓ π r² h. Sphere: V = \(\frac{4}{3}\) π r³, SA = 4 π r². Pyramid: V = ⅓ × base area × h.
A hemisphere is half a sphere, so halve the sphere volume.
Reverse: to find a missing length, substitute the numbers and rearrange. Working in multiples of π keeps it exact.

11.94 is r², not r. Take the square root: r = √11.94 = 3.5 cm.

guided_steps.pre: Cone in π units: ⅓ × 3² × 9 = ⅓ × 81 =

misconceptions.message: You divided the wrong way: cone ÷ cylinder = ⅓. The question asks how many times bigger the cylinder is, so cylinder ÷ cone = 3.

gold.hint: Big cone volume minus the small top cone. Cutting at half height halves the radius too.

guided_steps.pre: Big cone in π units: ⅓ × 6² × 12 = ⅓ × 432 =
Small cone in π units: ⅓ × 3² × 6 = ⅓ × 54 =
Subtract, then multiply by π: (144 − 18) × π =

Subtract the removed tip: 144π − 18π = 126π = 396 cm³. The whole cone alone is 452.4.

gold.hint: The cylinder has radius 5 and height 10. Empty space = cylinder − sphere.

guided_steps.say: The sphere touches the cylinder all round, so the cylinder has radius 5 and height 10 (the diameter). Empty space = cylinder − sphere.

guided_steps.done: So the empty space is 261.8 cm³.

guided_steps.pre: Check: the gap is exactly a third of the cylinder, 250π ÷ 3 rounds to

misconceptions.message: That is the whole cylinder. The empty space is what is left after the sphere is removed: 250π − \(\frac{500\pi}{3}\) = \(\frac{250\pi}{3}\) = 261.8 cm³.

guided_steps.say: Volume of a cuboid is length × width × height. Multiply all three.

misconceptions.message: 108 cm² is the surface area, 2(lw + lh + wh). Volume is 6 × 4 × 3 = 72 cm³.

guided_steps.pre: Compare: the surface area would be 6 × 25 =
guided_steps.done: 150 is the surface area; the volume is 125 cm³.

bronze.hint: A cube has 6 identical square faces: find one, then times by 6.
bronze.display: Diagram not drawn accurately Find the surface area of a cube with side length 4 cm.

guided_steps.say: A cube has 6 identical square faces. Find one face, then multiply by 6.

guided_steps.done: 64 is the volume; the surface area is 96 cm².

misconceptions.message: 64 cm³ is the volume (4³). Surface area = 6 × 4² = 6 × 16 = 96 cm².

bronze.hint: Volume of any prism is the cross-section area times the length.
bronze.display: Diagram not drawn accurately A prism has a cross-section area of 15 cm² and length 8 cm. Find its volume.

guided_steps.say: Volume of any prism is the cross-section area times the length.

guided_steps.done: Back to the 15 cm² cross-section, so V = 120 cm³.

misconceptions.message: Multiply, do not add: volume of a prism = cross-section area × length = 15 × 8 = 120 cm³.

bronze.hint: Find the triangle's area first, then multiply by the length.
bronze.display: Diagram not drawn accurately A triangular prism has a triangle base 6 cm, triangle height 4 cm and length 7 cm. Find its volume.

guided_steps.say: A triangular prism's cross-section is the triangle. Find its area, then multiply by the length.

guided_steps.done: Back to the 12 cm² triangle, so V = 84 cm³.

misconceptions.message: The cross-section is a triangle, so halve base × height: ½ × 6 × 4 = 12, then 12 × 7 = 84 cm³. Forgetting the half gives 168.

bronze.hint: Surface area of a cuboid is 2(lw + lh + wh). Find the three different faces first.

guided_steps.say: Surface area of a cuboid is 2(lw + lh + wh). Find the three different faces first.

guided_steps.hint: That is half the surface area.

misconceptions.message: 30 cm³ is the volume. Surface area = 2(lw + lh + wh) = 2(15 + 10 + 6) = 62 cm².

bronze.display: Diagram not drawn accurately A cuboid has volume 180 cm³. Its length is 10 cm and width is 6 cm. Find the height.

guided_steps.say: Volume = length × width × height, so height = volume ÷ (length × width).

guided_steps.pre: Divide the volume by the base area: 180 ÷ 60 =

guided_steps.done: Back to 180 cm³, so h = 3 cm.

misconceptions.message: Divide by BOTH known lengths: height = 180 ÷ (10 × 6) = 180 ÷ 60 = 3 cm. Dividing by only the 10 gives 18.

guided_steps.hint: 20π is about 62.8, to the nearest whole number.

guided_steps.pre: The two ends, 2πr², in π units: 2 × 3² =
The curved side, 2πrh, in π units: 2 × 3 × 10 =
Add and multiply by π: (18 + 60) × π =

silver.hint: Volume of a cone is one third of π r² h.
silver.display: Diagram not drawn accurately A cone has radius 4 cm and height 9 cm. Find the volume to 1 d.p.

guided_steps.say: Volume of a cone is \(\frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h\). Build the \(\pi r^2 h\) part, then take a third.

misconceptions.message: That is the full cylinder. A cone is one third: V = ⅓ × π × 4² × 9 = 48π = 150.8 cm³.

silver.hint: Volume of a sphere is four thirds of π r³. Cube the radius first.
silver.display: Diagram not drawn accurately A sphere has radius 3 cm. Find the volume to 1 d.p.

guided_steps.say: Volume of a sphere is \(\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3\). Cube the radius first.

guided_steps.pre: Check: four thirds × π × 27 rounds to

misconceptions.message: Cube the radius, do not square it: V = \(\frac{4}{3}\) × π × 3³ = 36π = 113.1 cm³. Squaring gives 37.7.

silver.hint: A hemisphere is half a sphere: find the full sphere, then halve it.
silver.display: Diagram not drawn accurately A hemisphere has radius 5 cm. Find the volume to 1 d.p.

guided_steps.say: A hemisphere is half a sphere. Find the full sphere's volume, then halve it.

guided_steps.pre: Check: two thirds × π × 125 rounds to

misconceptions.message: A hemisphere is HALF a sphere: V = ½ × \(\frac{4}{3}\) × π × 5³ = 261.8 cm³. The full sphere (523.6) is double.

silver.hint: Volume of a pyramid is one third of base area × height.
silver.display: Diagram not drawn accurately A pyramid has a square base of side 6 cm and height 10 cm. Find the volume.

guided_steps.say: Volume of a pyramid is \(\frac{1}{3} \times\) base area \(\times h\). Find the base area first.

misconceptions.message: That is base area × height with no third. A pyramid is one third: V = ⅓ × 36 × 10 = 120 cm³.

silver.hint: Surface area of a sphere is 4 π r². Square the radius first.

guided_steps.say: Surface area of a sphere is \(4\pi r^2\). Square the radius first.

misconceptions.message: That is the volume. Surface area = 4 π r² = 4 × π × 4² = 64π = 201.1 cm².
